summary: KERNEL CONTEST: The GDPR's 'Right to Erasure' (the codified legal kernel) read expansively as an individual privacy fundamental right versus read critically as an incumbent competitive moat and censorship mechanism. Each reading emits different beneficiary structures and defines the limits of data sovereignty from the exact same text[cite: 2, 3].

KERNEL CONTEST: The Bhagavad Gita's discourse at Kurukshetra (the shared textual kernel) read orthodoxly as a literal mandate for caste duty and justified physical violence versus read allegorically (e.g., by Gandhi) as a metaphor for internal spiritual struggle. The contest determines the text's behavioral constraints and authority grounding[cite: 2].

KERNEL CONTEST: The 1923 Treaty of Lausanne's minority protections (the fixed legal kernel) read restrictively by the host state (minimizing institutional autonomy and property rights) versus read expansively by the Patriarchate and international bodies as guaranteeing full religious continuity. An inter-institutional contest over the exact limits of a shared commitment[cite: 2, 3].

KERNEL CONTEST: The reciprocal blood-feud and honor obligations of early Germanic societies (a practice-based norm kernel) read by participants as a necessary, self-enforcing coordination mechanism for stateless justice versus read by emerging central/church authorities as a destructive cycle of extraction. The contest centers on which framework holds legitimate authority to adjudicate violence[cite: 2].
